claims.text: Moderate increases in Al content introduce an optimal level of atomic-size misfit and lattice strain.
Al-induced lattice strain modifies the relative free energies of competing phases.
An optimal level of lattice strain stabilizes a balanced FCC+BCC dual-phase microstructure.
A balanced FCC+BCC microstructure underpins a combination of high-temperature strength, environmental resistance, radiation tolerance, and cryogenic toughness.
The equiatomic Al-Co-Cr-Fe-Ni baseline has a homogeneous phase distribution.
The controlled comparison varies Al content by plus or minus 5% around the equiatomic composition while nominally holding the other elemental amounts constant.
The samples will be exposed at 1000-1200 degrees Celsius and then rapidly quenched.
X-ray diffraction peak broadening can be used here to quantify lattice distortion or strain.
Transmission electron microscopy can identify the resulting microstructural phases.
Variations in Al content alter atomic-size mismatch and generate controlled lattice strain.
The strain state promotes either a single-phase solid solution or an FCC+BCC dual-phase structure by changing relative phase free energies.
Moderate Al increases will produce a dual-phase microstructure relative to the equiatomic baseline.
The Al-enriched dual-phase alloys will have improved high-temperature mechanical strength and cryogenic toughness relative to the equiatomic baseline.
The Al-enriched dual-phase alloys will retain radiation tolerance and environmental resistance.
Al-induced misfit beyond the controlled range will cause over-segregation or excessive phase separation.
Over-segregation or excessive phase separation will degrade at least one target property.
The proposed mechanism is bounded to approximately plus or minus 5% Al variation and processing at 1000-1200 degrees Celsius followed by rapid quenching.
Changes in electronic interactions caused by varying Al may confound attribution of phase stability to lattice strain.
A lack of systematic correlation between lattice distortion or phase fraction and the target properties relative to the baseline would falsify the proposed governing mechanism.
